quests.hint: BEGINNING YOUR VERY FIRST DAY OF EMPLOYMENT SOMEWHERE NEW
quests.explanation: START A JOB means to begin working somewhere new. START pairs with the beginning of something ongoing, such as a job, a course, or a project.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: begin a JOB at the very moment
open a JOB position for yourself
quests.contextSentence: She was nervous but excited to start her first ___ at the marketing firm.

quests.hint: FINISHING SOMETHING BEFORE THE TIME YOUR BOSS OR CLIENT EXPECTS IT
quests.explanation: MEET A DEADLINE means to finish something on time. MEET is the standard verb here — you meet a deadline, meet a target, or meet someone's expectations.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this workplace pressure.
wrongCollocations: catch a DEADLINE like a bus
win a DEADLINE by finishing first
quests.contextSentence: The whole team stayed late on Friday to meet the project ___.

quests.hint: STOPPING WORK FOR A SHORT WHILE TO REST OR GET COFFEE
quests.explanation: TAKE A BREAK means to pause your work briefly to rest. TAKE combines with periods of rest — take a break, take a nap, take some time off.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this workplace routine.
wrongCollocations: make a BREAK during work by force
have a BREAK created for you
quests.contextSentence: After two hours of meetings, everyone was relieved to finally take a short ___.

quests.hint: DOING EXACTLY WHAT YOU TOLD SOMEONE YOU WOULD DO
quests.explanation: KEEP A PROMISE means to follow through on something you said you'd do. KEEP pairs with commitments you honor, unlike BREAK, which describes failing to honor them.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: hold a PROMISE in your hands
carry a PROMISE around with you
quests.contextSentence: Even though it was inconvenient, he wanted to keep his ___ to help her move.

quests.hint: FAILING TO DO SOMETHING AFTER TELLING SOMEONE YOU WOULD
quests.explanation: BREAK A PROMISE is the opposite of keeping one — it means failing to do what you said you would. BREAK also pairs with rules and records, describing something no longer being honored or standing.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this disappointing situation.
wrongCollocations: destroy a PROMISE physically
cancel a PROMISE like an event
quests.contextSentence: She felt terrible after having to break her ___ to visit her grandmother that weekend.

quests.hint: FINDING THE ANSWER TO SOMETHING THAT'S BEEN CAUSING TROUBLE
quests.explanation: SOLVE A PROBLEM means to find a solution to it. SOLVE pairs specifically with problems, puzzles, and mysteries — things that require figuring something out.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that completes this problem-solving action.
wrongCollocations: fix a PROBLEM like a broken machine only
repair a PROBLEM with tools
quests.contextSentence: The engineers worked all weekend trying to solve the technical ___.

quests.hint: FOCUSING YOUR MIND CLOSELY ON SOMETHING SO YOU DON'T MISS DETAILS
quests.explanation: PAY ATTENTION means to focus your mind on something. PAY combines with ATTENTION in a fixed way — you don't say 'give attention' in the same everyday sense, even though GIVE works with many other nouns.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make ATTENTION toward someone
do ATTENTION during class
quests.contextSentence: The teacher asked the students to pay close ___ during the safety demonstration.

quests.hint: WRITING DOWN KEY POINTS WHILE SOMEONE IS SPEAKING SO YOU DON'T FORGET
quests.explanation: TAKE NOTES means to write down important information as you hear it. TAKE pairs with NOTES the way it does with many things you record or capture, like take a photo or take notes.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this study or meeting habit.
wrongCollocations: write NOTES onto paper only physically
make NOTES appear from nowhere
quests.contextSentence: During the lecture, most students were busy taking ___ on their laptops.

quests.hint: STARTING TO SPEAK BEFORE SOMEONE ELSE HAS FINISHED WHAT THEY WERE SAYING
quests.explanation: INTERRUPT A CONVERSATION means to break into it before someone finishes speaking. INTERRUPT pairs with ongoing activities you disturb, such as a conversation, a meeting, or a class.
quests.instruction: Select the word that completes this communication mistake.
wrongCollocations: break a CONVERSATION into pieces physically
stop a CONVERSATION permanently by force
quests.contextSentence: It's rude to interrupt a ___ just because you disagree with what's being said.

quests.hint: SLOWLY DEVELOPING A CLOSE CONNECTION WITH SOMEONE OVER TIME
quests.explanation: BUILD A RELATIONSHIP means to develop it gradually, often through trust and shared experience. BUILD is used for things that grow stronger over time, such as a relationship, trust, or a career.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make a RELATIONSHIP overnight instantly
do a RELATIONSHIP with effort
quests.contextSentence: It takes years to build a strong ___ based on honesty and respect.

quests.hint: SUDDENLY DEVELOPING ROMANTIC FEELINGS FOR SOMEONE
quests.explanation: FALL IN LOVE is the fixed expression for developing romantic feelings, often unexpectedly. FALL IN suggests something that happens to you, rather than something you plan or control.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this romantic expression.
wrongCollocations: make LOVE happen on schedule
build LOVE step by step slowly
quests.contextSentence: They met at a coffee shop and, within weeks, had completely fallen in ___.

quests.hint: FINDING A WAY TO END A DISAGREEMENT SO BOTH SIDES ARE SATISFIED
quests.explanation: RESOLVE A CONFLICT means to settle a disagreement peacefully. RESOLVE is more formal than SOLVE and is used specifically for disputes, arguments, or tension between people.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this peacemaking effort.
wrongCollocations: win a CONFLICT by force
finish a CONFLICT with a trophy
quests.contextSentence: The manager stepped in to help resolve the ___ between the two team members.

quests.hint: ARRANGING A SPECIFIC TIME TO SEE A DOCTOR IN ADVANCE
quests.explanation: BOOK AN APPOINTMENT means to arrange a specific time in advance, usually by phone or online. BOOK is used for reserving a slot — an appointment, a table, a ticket.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: reserve an APPOINTMENT like a hotel room
order an APPOINTMENT online for delivery
quests.contextSentence: After the pain didn't go away, she decided to book a doctor's ___.

quests.hint: GRADUALLY GETTING BETTER AND RETURNING TO NORMAL HEALTH AFTER BEING SICK
quests.explanation: RECOVER FROM AN ILLNESS means to get better after being sick. RECOVER FROM is followed by whatever you're getting better after — an illness, an injury, or even a difficult experience.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this healing process.
wrongCollocations: fix an ILLNESS like a machine
solve an ILLNESS with logic
quests.contextSentence: It took him almost a month to fully recover from the ___.

quests.hint: STICKING TO A SPECIFIC WAY OF EATING FOR HEALTH OR WEIGHT REASONS
quests.explanation: FOLLOW A DIET means to stick to a particular eating plan. FOLLOW pairs with plans and instructions you commit to over time, such as a diet, a routine, or advice.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this health-related habit.
wrongCollocations: obey a DIET like a strict rule enforced by others
chase a DIET around
quests.contextSentence: Her doctor recommended she follow a low-sugar ___ for a few months.

quests.hint: SUPPORTING YOURSELF FINANCIALLY THROUGH REGULAR PAID WORK
quests.explanation: EARN A LIVING means to make enough money through work to support yourself. EARN combines with LIVING in this fixed phrase, distinct from earning a single payment or wage.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make a LIVING instantly overnight
win a LIVING through luck
quests.contextSentence: He gave up his hobby to earn a proper ___ as a full-time electrician.

quests.hint: PUTTING YOUR MONEY INTO SOMETHING, HOPING IT GROWS IN VALUE OVER TIME
quests.explanation: INVEST IN STOCKS means to put money into shares, hoping for future profit. INVEST IN is followed by whatever you're putting money into — stocks, property, or a business.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this financial decision.
wrongCollocations: spend on STOCKS without any thought
buy STOCKS randomly for fun
quests.contextSentence: After reading several books on finance, she decided to invest in ___ for the first time.

quests.hint: OWING MORE MONEY THAN YOU CAN COMFORTABLY PAY BACK
quests.explanation: GO INTO DEBT means to start owing money you haven't repaid. GO INTO describes entering a difficult financial state, unlike GET INTO, which is used more casually for hobbies or habits.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this financial warning.
wrongCollocations: fall into DEBT physically like a hole
catch DEBT like an illness
quests.contextSentence: Without a clear budget, it's easy to go into ___ during the holiday season.

quests.hint: INSTALLING THE NEWEST VERSION OF A PROGRAM ON YOUR PHONE
quests.explanation: UPDATE AN APP means to install its newest version. UPDATE pairs with software and systems — you update an app, your phone, or a computer program.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: renew an APP like a subscription
refresh an APP like a drink
quests.contextSentence: The banking ___ needed to update before it would let her log in again.

quests.hint: SAVING A COPY OF YOUR FILES SOMEWHERE SAFE IN CASE THE ORIGINAL IS LOST
quests.explanation: BACK UP YOUR DATA means to save an extra copy of your files for safety. BACK UP is the standard phrasal verb for this precaution, whether the data is photos, documents, or contacts.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this safety habit.
wrongCollocations: copy DATA by hand physically only
duplicate DATA using scissors
quests.contextSentence: Before updating the software, make sure to back up your ___ just in case.

quests.hint: WHEN A DEVICE'S POWER REACHES ZERO AND IT SHUTS OFF
quests.explanation: RUN OUT OF BATTERY means the device's power supply is completely used up. RUN OUT OF is used broadly for anything that gets fully used up — battery, time, patience, or money.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this frustrating tech moment.
wrongCollocations: finish BATTERY completely by choice
empty BATTERY on purpose
quests.contextSentence: Right in the middle of the call, her phone ran out of ___.

quests.hint: ARRANGING A SPECIFIC TIME FOR PEOPLE TO DISCUSS SOMETHING AT WORK
quests.explanation: SCHEDULE A MEETING means to arrange a time for it in advance. SCHEDULE is common in professional English for planning meetings, calls, or appointments ahead of time.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: make a MEETING happen without planning
build a MEETING like a structure
quests.contextSentence: Could we schedule a quick ___ tomorrow morning to go over the budget?

quests.hint: MOVING A PLANNED MEETING OR VISIT TO A DIFFERENT TIME
quests.explanation: RESCHEDULE AN APPOINTMENT means to change its time or date after it's already been booked. RESCHEDULE implies something was already planned and now needs to move, unlike SCHEDULE, which means planning it for the first time.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this scheduling change.
wrongCollocations: remake an APPOINTMENT from scratch entirely
redo an APPOINTMENT like homework
quests.contextSentence: Something came up at work, so I had to reschedule my dentist ___.

quests.hint: COMPLETELY CALLING OFF A BOOKING YOU NO LONGER NEED
quests.explanation: CANCEL A RESERVATION means to call it off entirely rather than change its time. CANCEL is the outright removal of a plan, unlike RESCHEDULE, which simply moves it to another time.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this booking situation.
wrongCollocations: delete a RESERVATION from a table physically
erase a RESERVATION with a pencil
quests.contextSentence: Since the trip was postponed, they had to cancel their hotel ___.

quests.hint: RESERVING YOUR SEAT ON A PLANE BEFORE THE TRIP
quests.explanation: BOOK A FLIGHT means to reserve a seat on a plane in advance. BOOK is used broadly for travel reservations — a flight, a hotel room, or a rental car.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: reserve a FLIGHT like ordering food
order a FLIGHT for delivery
quests.contextSentence: Prices go up closer to summer, so it's smart to book your ___ early.

quests.hint: PUTTING YOUR CLOTHES AND BELONGINGS INTO LUGGAGE BEFORE A TRIP
quests.explanation: PACK A SUITCASE means to fill it with what you need for a trip. PACK pairs with any container you fill for travel — a suitcase, a bag, or a backpack.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this pre-trip task.
wrongCollocations: load a SUITCASE like a truck
build a SUITCASE from empty boxes
quests.contextSentence: The night before the flight, she stayed up late packing her ___.

quests.hint: PASSING A CHECKPOINT AT THE AIRPORT WHERE YOUR BAGS ARE SCANNED
quests.explanation: GO THROUGH SECURITY means to pass the airport checkpoint where bags and passengers are checked. GO THROUGH is used for passing a required process or checkpoint, not just walking somewhere.
quests.instruction: Select the word that fits this airport process.
wrongCollocations: pass through SECURITY like a door only physically
cross SECURITY like a finish line
quests.contextSentence: We arrived early because the line to go through ___ can take almost an hour.

quests.hint: FORMING NEW SOCIAL CONNECTIONS, ESPECIALLY IN AN UNFAMILIAR PLACE
quests.explanation: MAKE FRIENDS means to form new friendships, especially somewhere new. MAKE pairs with FRIENDS in this fixed way, distinct from inviting people you already know.
quests.instruction: Find the word that naturally completes the pair.
wrongCollocations: build FRIENDS like a wall
create FRIENDS out of nothing artificially
quests.contextSentence: Moving to a new city made it hard for him to make ___ at first.

quests.hint: CONTINUING TO CALL, TEXT, OR VISIT SOMEONE AFTER YOU STOP SEEING THEM REGULARLY
quests.explanation: KEEP IN TOUCH means to continue communicating with someone over time. KEEP IN TOUCH is a fixed expression, often used when people are about to be apart, such as after graduation or a move.
quests.instruction: Choose the word that completes this parting expression.
wrongCollocations: stay in TOUCH by physically touching someone
hold in TOUCH with your hands
quests.contextSentence: Before graduation, they all promised to keep in ___ no matter where life took them.

quests.hint: HAVING A FRIENDLY, EASYGOING RELATIONSHIP WITH THE PEOPLE YOU WORK WITH
quests.explanation: GET ALONG WITH YOUR COLLEAGUES means to have a friendly, cooperative relationship with them. GET ALONG WITH is used for describing how well two people or groups interact day to day.
quests.instruction: Pick the word that fits this workplace relationship.
wrongCollocations: walk along with your COLLEAGUES physically every day
travel along with your COLLEAGUES everywhere
quests.contextSentence: She's always found it easy to get along with her ___, even during busy weeks.
